This glossary covers both the concepts returned by gifter and the technical
language used to curate and compile its reference database. Resource-specific
terms describe how gifter interprets them; they are not replacements for the
resources' own documentation.

The short form of the evidence hierarchy is:

```text
Frame --resolves by metadata--> GIFT

metabolic GIFT
  -> route -> reaction -> enzyme system -> component -> marker

structural, regulatory or defense GIFT
  -> architecture, circuit or mechanism
  -> function -> system -> component -> marker
```

A frame begins the analytical browsing path, but it is not a biological parent
of a GIFT and stores no fixed list of GIFT identifiers.

## GIFT and analysis concepts

### Anchor

A curated input or output molecule defining the boundary of a metabolic GIFT.
Only declared anchors connect GIFTs. An internal reaction participant is not an
anchor merely because it occurs in the chemistry.

### Architecture

One complete curated implementation of a structural GIFT. Architectures are
alternatives under OR logic; every required function within one architecture is
combined under AND logic.

### Assessability

Whether a genome is complete enough for its lack of support for a GIFT to be
informative. Assessability may change a denominator or make an absence
indeterminate. It can never turn an unsupported GIFT into a supported one.

### Bounded frame

A frame whose curation deliberately intends to enumerate a biologically closed
set. Only a bounded frame licenses a coverage fraction over all its members. An
open and growing catalogue is not bounded.

### Circuit

One complete curated implementation of a regulatory GIFT.

### Compartment

The `extracellular` or `cytoplasmic` qualifier on a declared anchor. It makes
transport and possible cross-genome compatibility explicit without introducing
compartment-aware stoichiometry or inferring protein localization.

### Complete

The Boolean state reached when at least one entire curated implementation of a
GIFT is supported. Completeness means encoded capability under the model, not
expression, activity, flux or phenotype.

### Component

One required protein role within an enzyme or machinery system. Every required
component of a system is combined under AND logic; any accepted marker may
support a component under OR logic.

### Defense mechanism

One complete curated implementation of a defense GIFT.

### Facet

A curated classification used to describe or select GIFTs, anchors or related
entities. A facet does not decide the completeness model; `gift_type` does.

### Frame (reference frame)

The comparison set and denominator within which a quantitative trait is read.
A named frame stores metadata filters and interpretation limits, then resolves
its current GIFT members against a database release. It never stores a list of
`gift_id` values.

### Function

In a structural, regulatory or defense model, one required biological role
within an architecture, circuit or mechanism. It is the machinery analogue of
a metabolic reaction and is implemented by any one complete system.

### GIFT

A genome-inferred functional trait: a biologically meaningful capability whose
genomic support is evaluated through an explicit, curated and traceable
completeness model.

### GIFT type

One of `metabolic`, `structural`, `regulatory` or `defense`. It selects the
completeness model and determines which source tables may attach to a GIFT. It
is part of the core ontology, not a facet.

### Internal intermediate

A reaction participant inside a metabolic route that is not a declared anchor.
Shared internal intermediates do not connect GIFTs.

### Marker

A namespaced genomic observation used as evidence for a component. Marker
identity is the pair `namespace + accession`; a marker is never itself a GIFT,
reaction or function.

### Mechanism

See **defense mechanism**.

### Mode

The direction or role of a metabolic GIFT, such as `anabolic`, `catabolic`,
`transport` or `interconversion`. Non-metabolic GIFTs do not have a mode.

### Reaction

A biochemical transformation, identified by its stable `reaction_id` and by a
Rhea master wherever Rhea covers the chemistry. Its contextual direction is
stored on route membership rather than by changing reaction identity.

### Route

A curated minimal set of required reactions connecting a metabolic GIFT's
declared input and output anchors. Routes are alternatives under OR logic; all
required reactions within a route are combined under AND logic.

### Supported

Backed by the observed markers at the relevant level of the completeness
hierarchy. Support propagates only through the declared OR/AND rules. It is not
evidence of expression or activity.

### System

One complete protein implementation of a reaction or machinery function. A
system may be a single protein or several jointly required components.

### Traceability

The ability to explain a GIFT call through its selected implementation,
reactions or functions, systems, components, observed markers and supplied gene
identifiers.

## Marker and profile terminology

### Accession

A stable identifier assigned by an external resource, such as `K00764`,
`PF01752` or `NF040708.3`. In gifter it is interpreted together with its
namespace. Similar-looking strings from different namespaces are not
interchangeable.

### Bit score

A log-odds score describing how strongly a sequence matches a profile HMM.
Scores are meaningful only with the relevant model, thresholds and coverage;
gifter does not treat a high score alone as proof that a marker is suitable for
a biological claim.

### Domain

A conserved region of a protein that may occur in proteins with different
overall functions. A domain-level match often supports structural homology but
not the specific activity of a complete protein. In NCBIfam, the `domain`
family type does not carry the one-function assertion required for automatic
admission by grade.

### Equivalog

An NCBIfam family type asserting that the proteins recognized by the profile
share one specific function. gifter admits `equivalog` as an eligible grade,
but still checks the biological annotation, reaction direction, taxonomic
scope and specificity before accepting the profile as marker evidence.

### Equivalog domain

An NCBIfam profile covering a function-specific domain rather than necessarily
the full protein. It carries NCBIfam's one-function assertion and is an eligible
grade in gifter, but the curator must still verify that the domain is sufficient
evidence for the component being claimed.

### Gathering threshold

The model-specific score cutoff curated for accepting members of a profile HMM
family. It should be used with the profile release it belongs to; it is not a
universal score cutoff shared across models.

### Homolog

A sequence related to another sequence by common ancestry. Homology alone does
not establish that two proteins perform the same function.

### Ortholog

Homologous genes related through speciation rather than duplication. Orthology
can support functional inference, but an orthology group may still be broader
than a reaction, substrate or machinery role curated by gifter.

### PfamAutoEq

An automated NCBIfam family type derived from a Pfam model. gifter does not
treat it as an admitted equivalog grade; the label does not supply the curated
one-function guarantee required for `NCBIFAM` marker admission.

### Profile HMM

A profile hidden Markov model representing position-specific patterns learned
from a multiple sequence alignment. Searches produce scores and alignments
against which model-specific thresholds and coverage requirements are applied.

### Sequence coverage

The fraction of the profile or target sequence included in an alignment. It
helps distinguish a complete family match from a short local match but does not
by itself establish functional specificity.

### Subfamily

A subset within a broader protein family. The word alone does not guarantee one
specific biochemical function. In NCBIfam, `subfamily` is a distinct family
type and is not one of the two equivalog grades gifter admits.

### Versioned accession

An accession whose suffix identifies a particular build of its model, such as
`NF040708.3`. For NCBIfam markers the suffix is part of identity because model
alignments and cutoffs can change between versions.

## External identifiers and resources

### CAZy and dbCAN

CAZy classifies carbohydrate-active enzymes into families and, where available,
subfamilies. dbCAN provides sequence models and annotation tools for those
classes. A broad CAZy family can contain several characterized activities, so
family membership is not automatically evidence for one substrate-specific
GIFT.

### ChEBI identifier

An identifier for a chemical entity. gifter uses ChEBI identifiers for declared
anchors where possible; it does not use them to turn every internal metabolite
into an anchor.

### EC number

An Enzyme Commission classification of catalysed activity. An EC number may be
incomplete or may group chemistry more broadly than one curated Rhea reaction,
so it is evidence and cross-reference material rather than a substitute for
reaction curation.

### KEGG Orthology (KO)

A KEGG functional orthology group identified by a `K` accession. KOs are a
major marker namespace in gifter, but each KO is checked against the specificity
of the component and reaction it is proposed to support.

### Namespace

The identifier system in which an accession has meaning, such as `KO`, `EC`,
`PFAM`, `TIGRFAM`, `NCBIFAM` or `CAZY`. Marker identity is always the namespace
and accession together.

### NCBIfam

NCBI's collection of protein family profile HMMs used by tools including PGAP
and exposed through other annotation systems. gifter pins a named release,
requires versioned accessions, and admits only the `equivalog` and
`equivalog_domain` grades after biological review.

### Pfam

A database of protein families and domains represented by profile HMMs. A Pfam
match can be strong evidence of family or domain membership without necessarily
identifying the precise activity required by a GIFT.

### Rhea master

Rhea's stable master identifier for a biochemical reaction independent of the
direction in which a particular route uses it. gifter stores route orientation
separately as `forward` or `reverse`.

### TIGRFAM

A historical protein-family namespace whose `TIGR` accessions are still used by
some annotation resources. In gifter an unversioned `TIGRFAM` accession and a
versioned `NCBIFAM` model derived from a TIGRFAM lineage are distinct markers.

## Curation and database-generation terms

### Candidate

A capability, route, architecture or marker under investigation. A candidate
is not part of the ontology and cannot produce a call until it has passed
curation, validation and release.

### Confidence

A curated description of the strength or ambiguity of accepted evidence.
Confidence summarizes evidence quality; it does not replace the Boolean
completeness result or promote an unsupported GIFT.

### Database source

The human-reviewable TSV files from which the runtime SQLite database is
compiled. They are the biological source of truth; SQLite is a generated
artifact.

### Deferral

A decision that a candidate is worth revisiting but is presently blocked. A
deferral records the blocker and the evidence or resource change that would
retrigger investigation.

### Diagnostic proxy

A provisional marker set used to measure prevalence, disagreement or likely
failure modes during curation. A proxy is not a GIFT definition and is never
silently promoted into one.

### Evidence type

The kind of relationship supporting a component-to-marker assertion, such as
orthology or sequence-family evidence. It records what the marker represents;
it is distinct from evidence confidence.

### Marker specificity

How narrowly a marker identifies the component or chemistry being claimed. The
specificity of a GIFT may never exceed the specificity of the evidence that
supports it.

### Marker-specificity screen

A reproducible comparison used to identify over-broad accessions, coverage
gaps, conflicts between resources or profiles worth manual review. A screen
creates evidence for curation; it does not automatically admit its candidates.

### Provenance

The recorded origin of a biological fact or curation decision: resource,
release, retrieval date, literature or gifter-specific interpretation. Imported
facts are kept distinct from gifter's choices of boundaries, implementations
and claim scope.

### Refusal

A recorded decision not to curate a candidate because the evidence cannot
support the proposed claim or the claim violates the ontology. A refusal is a
durable curation result rather than an undocumented gap.

### Retrigger

A concrete change that justifies reopening a deferred or refused assessment,
such as a new specific marker, characterized chemistry or a resource release
that resolves the recorded blocker. Repeating the same request is not a
retrigger.

### SQLite artifact

The compiled, read-only runtime representation of the curated source tables. It
is regenerated after source changes and is never edited manually.

For the end-to-end process that connects these terms, see
[How a GIFT is built](curating-a-gift.html).
